title: Engineering an icon
description: Analogue feeling meets a new level of engineering precision.

cars.name: McLaren F1
cars.description: The F1 placed its driver in the centre of a three-seat cabin and paired a carbon-fibre structure with a naturally aspirated BMW V12. Gordon Murray’s design pursued low weight and exceptional response. Its compact proportions, dihedral doors and carefully considered details made it a landmark of 1990s supercar engineering.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent standard 1995 F1 road cars. LM, GT and GTR variants, competition history and exceptional provenance have different values.

cars.name: Honda NSX
cars.description: Honda approached the mid-engined sports car with an emphasis on precision, visibility and everyday usability. The original NSX combined an aluminium body with a VTEC V6 behind the seats. Its low bonnet, pop-up headlights and wraparound rear lights gave advanced engineering a clean, restrained shape that still feels distinctive.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent 3.0-litre NSX coupés. Transmission, import specification, originality and maintenance history affect value; Type R and later 3.2-litre cars are excluded.

cars.name: Toyota Supra A80 Twin Turbo
cars.description: The fourth-generation Supra traded the angular lines of its predecessor for a rounded, muscular body and a driver-focused cockpit. The twin-turbocharged 2JZ-GTE straight-six became central to its reputation. A long bonnet, distinctive rear lights and prominent rear wing helped make the A80 one of the decade’s best-known Japanese performance cars.

cost.basis: Indicative GBP range using rounded good-to-excellent figures from the UK guide’s broader 1994 A80 coupé category. This is a proxy, not a turbo-specific appraisal; original twin-turbo manuals can command a premium.

cars.name: Dodge Viper RT/10
cars.description: The original Viper revived the idea of a big-engined American roadster with an uncompromising character. Its long bonnet covered an 8.0-litre V10, while side-mounted exhausts and broad rear wings gave the body a purposeful stance. The early RT/10’s open cockpit and simple controls kept the driving experience direct.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP range around The Classic Valuer’s roughly £37,000 RT/10 median. Its worldwide, multi-year sales data is a broad reference rather than a 1994 UK condition-specific appraisal; imports, mileage and originality affect value.

cars.name: Lamborghini Diablo
cars.description: The Diablo succeeded the Countach in 1990 with a more rounded interpretation of Lamborghini’s dramatic mid-engined supercar. A 5.7-litre V12, scissor doors and wide rear bodywork preserved the theatre. This early rear-wheel-drive version represents the original design before all-wheel-drive VT models and later styling changes expanded the family.

cost.basis: UK guide range for good to excellent early 5.7-litre Diablo coupés. VT, SE30, SV, roadster and later 6.0-litre variants are separate markets.
